verses.37:28: And the Midianite men, the merchants, passed by; and they drew and lifted Joseph up out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of gold; and they brought Joseph down to Egypt.
verses.37:29: Then Reuben returned to the pit, and he did not see Joseph in the pit; and he tore his garments.
verses.37:30: And he returned to his brethren and said, "The lad is no more; and as for me, where shall I go now?"
verses.37:31: Then they took Joseph's tunic, slaughtered a kid of the goats, and stained the tunic with blood.
verses.37:32: And they sent the tunic of many colors and brought it to their father, and said, "We have found this; examine whether it is your son's tunic or not."
verses.37:33: And he recognized it and said, "It is my son's tunic! An evil wild beast has devoured him; a wild beast has carried off Joseph."
verses.37:34: Then Jacob tore his garments, and put sackcloth upon his loins, and mourned for his son for some days.
verses.37:35: And all his sons and daughters gathered together and came to comfort him, yet he refused to be comforted, saying, "I shall go down to my son in mourning to Hades." Thus his father wept for him.
verses.37:36: Meanwhile the Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, the eunuch of Pharaoh, the chief cook.
verses.38:1: Now it came to pass at that time that Judah went down from his brethren and came to a certain Adullamite man whose name was Hirah.
verses.38:2: And there Judah saw a Canaanite man's daughter, whose name was Shua; and he took her and went in to her.
verses.38:3: And she conceived and bore a son, and called his name Er.
verses.38:4: And she conceived again and bore a son, and called his name Onan.
verses.38:5: And she bore yet another son, and called his name Shelah; now she was in Chezib when she bore them.
verses.38:6: And Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, whose name was Tamar.
verses.38:7: Now Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked before the Lord, and God slew him.
verses.38:8: Then Judah said to Onan, "Go in to your brother's wife and perform the duty of a brother-in-law to her, and raise up seed for your brother."
verses.38:9: But Onan knew that the seed would not be his; and it came to pass, whenever he went in to his brother's wife, that he poured it out upon the ground so as not to give seed to his brother.
verses.38:10: And the deed appeared wicked before God, that he did this, and He put him to death also.
verses.38:11: Then Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, "Remain a widow in your father's house until Shelah my son is grown." For he said, "Lest he also die like his brethren." So Tamar departed and remained in her father's house.
verses.38:12: And the days were multiplied, and Shua the wife of Judah died; and when Judah was comforted, he went up to those who were shearing his sheep, he and Hirah his shepherd, the Adullamite, to Timnah.
verses.38:13: And it was told to Tamar his daughter-in-law, saying, "Behold, your father-in-law has gone up to Timnah to shear his sheep."
verses.38:14: So she put off from herself the garments of her widowhood, wrapped herself in a veil, and adorned herself, and sat at the gates of Enan, which is on the way to Timnah; for she saw that Shelah his son was grown, yet he had not given her to him as a wife.
verses.38:15: And when Judah saw her, he supposed her to be a harlot, for she had covered her face, and he did not recognize her.
verses.38:16: And he turned aside from the way to her and said to her, "Let me come in to you," for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, "What will you give me if you come in to me?"
verses.38:17: And he said, "I will send you a kid of the goats from the flock." And she said, "If you give a pledge until you send it."
verses.38:18: And he said, "What pledge shall I give you?" And she said, "Your signet ring, and the necklace, and the staff that is in your hand." So he gave them to her and went in to her, and she conceived by him.
verses.38:19: Then she arose and departed, and took off the veil from herself, and put on the garments of her widowhood.
verses.38:20: And Judah sent the kid of the goats by the hand of his shepherd, the Adullamite, to receive the pledge back from the woman; but he did not find her.
verses.38:21: Then he asked the men of that place, "Where is the harlot who was in Enan by the wayside?" And they said, "There was no harlot here."
verses.38:22: So he returned to Judah and said, "I did not find her; and the men of that place say that there is no harlot here."
verses.38:23: And Judah said, "Let her keep them, lest we be mocked; I indeed have sent this kid, and you have not found her."
verses.38:24: And it came to pass after three months that it was told to Judah, saying, "Tamar your daughter-in-law has played the harlot, and behold, she is with child by harlotry." And Judah said, "Bring her out and let her be burned!"
verses.38:25: When she was brought out, she sent to her father-in-law, saying, "By the man to whom these belong, I am with child." And she said, "Examine whose are the signet ring, and the necklace, and this staff."
verses.38:26: And Judah recognized them and said, "Tamar is justified rather than I, because I did not give her to Shelah my son." And he did not know her again.
verses.38:27: Now it came to pass, when she gave birth, that there were twins in her womb.
verses.38:28: And it came to pass, while she was giving birth, that the one put out his hand; and the midwife took a scarlet thread and bound it upon his hand, saying, "This one will come out first."
verses.38:29: Then as he drew back his hand, immediately his brother came out. And she said, "Why has a barrier been broken through because of you?" And she called his name Perez.
verses.38:30: And after this his brother came out, on whose hand was the scarlet thread; and she called his name Zerah.
verses.39:1: Now Joseph was brought down to Egypt; and Potiphar, the eunuch of Pharaoh, the chief cook, an Egyptian man, purchased him from the hands of the Ishmaelites, who had brought him down there.
verses.39:2: And the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house with the Egyptian master.
verses.39:3: And his master knew that the Lord was with him, and that whatever he did, the Lord caused to prosper in his hands.
verses.39:4: So Joseph found favor before his master, and he was pleasing to him; and he appointed him over his house, and all things that belonged to him he placed into the hand of Joseph.
verses.39:5: Now it came to pass, after he was appointed over his house and over all that belonged to him, that the Lord blessed the house of the Egyptian for the sake of Joseph; and the blessing of the Lord was upon all his possessions, in the house and in the field.
verses.39:6: And he turned over all that belonged to him into the hands of Joseph, and he knew nothing of his own affairs except the bread which he himself ate. Now Joseph was handsome in form and exceedingly fair in appearance.
verses.39:7: And it came to pass after these things that his master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph, and said, "Lie with me."
verses.39:8: But he was unwilling, and said to his master's wife, "If my master knows nothing in his house because of me, and has given all that belongs to him into my hands,
verses.39:9: and surpasses me in nothing in his house, nor has he withheld anything from me except you, because you are his wife—how then shall I do this wicked thing and sin before God?"
verses.39:10: Now whenever she spoke to Joseph day after day, he did not listen to her to sleep with her, to be with her.
verses.39:11: And it came to pass on a certain such day that Joseph went into the house to do his work, and no one was inside the house.
verses.39:12: And she caught him by his garments, saying, "Lie with me." But leaving his garments behind, he fled and went outside.
verses.39:13: And it came to pass, when she saw that he had left his garments in her hands and had fled and gone outside,
verses.39:14: that she called those who were in the house and spoke to them, saying, "See, he has brought in to us a Hebrew servant to mock us; he came in to me, saying, 'Lie with me,' and I cried out with a loud voice.
verses.39:15: And when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried out, leaving his garments with me, he fled and went outside."
verses.39:16: And she kept the garments with her until the master came into his house.
verses.39:17: And she spoke to him according to these words, saying, "The Hebrew servant, whom you brought in to us, came in to me to mock me, and said to me, 'Lie with me.'
verses.39:18: And when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried out, he left his garments with me, and fled and went outside."
verses.39:19: Now it came to pass, when the master heard the words of his wife, which she spoke to him, saying, "Thus your servant has done to me," that he was enraged with wrath.
verses.39:20: And the master took Joseph and cast him into the stronghold, into the place where the prisoners of the king are held there in the stronghold.
verses.39:21: Yet the Lord was with Joseph and poured out mercy upon him, and granted him favor before the chief jailer.
verses.39:22: And the chief jailer committed the prison into the hand of Joseph, and all the captives who were in the prison, and all that they did there.
verses.39:23: The chief jailer knew nothing because of him; for all things were in the hand of Joseph, because the Lord was with him; and whatever he did, the Lord caused to prosper in his hands.
verses.40:1: Now it came to pass after these things that the chief cupbearer of the king of Egypt and the chief baker sinned against their lord, the king of Egypt.
verses.40:2: And Pharaoh was angry with his two eunuchs, with the chief cupbearer and with the chief baker;
verses.40:3: and he put them in custody with the chief jailer in the prison, in the place where Joseph had been led away.
verses.40:4: And the chief jailer entrusted them to Joseph, and he attended them; and they were in custody for some days.
verses.40:5: And both of them saw a dream, each one a dream in one night—a vision of his own dream—the chief cupbearer and the chief baker who belonged to the king of Egypt, who were in the prison.
verses.40:6: Now Joseph came in to them in the morning, and saw them, and they were troubled.
verses.40:7: And he asked the eunuchs of Pharaoh, who were with him in custody under his master, saying, "Why are your countenances downcast today?"
verses.40:8: And they said to him, "We have seen a dream, and there is no one to interpret it." Then Joseph said to them, "Is not the explanation of them through God? Tell me, therefore."
verses.40:9: So the chief cupbearer related his dream to Joseph and said, "In my sleep, there was a vine before me;
verses.40:10: and in the vine were three stems, and it was flourishing, having put forth shoots; the clusters of grapes were ripe.
verses.40:11: And the cup of Pharaoh was in my hand; and I took the grapes and pressed them into the cup, and I gave the cup into the hands of Pharaoh."
verses.40:12: And Joseph said to him, "This is its interpretation: the three stems are three days;
verses.40:13: yet three days, and Pharaoh will remember your office and will restore you to your office of chief cupbearer, and you shall give Pharaoh's cup into his hand according to your former office, as when you were cupbearer.
verses.40:14: But remember me on your own when it goes well with you, and show mercy to me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this stronghold;
verses.40:15: for indeed I was stolen away from the land of the Hebrews; and here I have done nothing, yet they cast me into this pit."
verses.40:16: Now the chief baker saw that he had interpreted rightly, and he said to Joseph, "I also saw a dream, and I thought I was carrying three baskets of coarse-wheat loaves upon my head;
verses.40:17: and in the uppermost basket were some of all kinds of foods which King Pharaoh eats, the work of a baker; and the birds of the air were devouring them from the basket upon my head."
verses.40:18: And Joseph answered and said to him, "This is its interpretation: the three baskets are three days;
verses.40:19: within three more days Pharaoh will take away your head from you, and will hang you upon a tree, and the birds of the air shall eat your flesh from off you."
verses.40:20: Now it came to pass on the third day, which was Pharaoh's birthday, that he made a banquet for all his servants; and he remembered the office of the chief cupbearer and the office of the chief baker in the midst of his servants.
verses.40:21: And he restored the chief cupbearer to his office, and he gave the cup into the hand of Pharaoh;
verses.40:22: but the chief baker he hanged, just as Joseph had interpreted to them.
verses.40:23: The chief cupbearer, however, did not remember Joseph, but forgot him.
verses.41:1: Now it came to pass after two full years that Pharaoh saw a dream: he supposed that he was standing by the river,
verses.41:2: and behold, as it were out of the river there came up seven cows, fair in appearance and choice in flesh, and they grazed in the reed grass.
verses.41:3: And seven other cows came up after them out of the river, ugly in appearance and lean in flesh, and the cows fed beside the bank of the river in the reed grass.
verses.41:4: And the seven cows that were ugly and lean in flesh devoured the seven cows that were fair in appearance and choice. Then Pharaoh awoke.
verses.41:5: And he dreamed a second time; and behold, seven ears of grain came up on one stalk, choice and good.
verses.41:6: And seven other ears of grain, thin and blighted by the wind, sprang up after them.
verses.41:7: And the seven thin and wind-blighted ears of grain swallowed up the seven choice and full ears of grain. Then Pharaoh awoke, and it was a dream.
verses.41:8: Now it came to pass in the morning that his soul was troubled; and he sent and called all the interpreters of Egypt and all its wise men. And Pharaoh recounted the dream to them, but there was no one who could declare it to Pharaoh.
verses.41:9: Then the chief cupbearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, "I call my sin to remembrance this day.
verses.41:10: Pharaoh was angry with his servants, and put us in custody in the house of the chief keeper of the prison, both me and the chief baker.
verses.41:11: And we saw a dream in one night, both he and I; each of us saw according to his own dream.
verses.41:12: Now there was with us there a young man, a Hebrew servant of the chief cook; and we told him, and he interpreted for us.
verses.41:13: And it came to pass that just as he interpreted for us, so indeed it happened: I was restored to my office, while he was hanged."
verses.41:14: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and brought him out of the stronghold; and they shaved him and changed his garment, and he came to Pharaoh.
verses.41:15: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I have seen a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it; yet I have heard it said concerning you that upon hearing dreams you interpret them."
verses.41:16: And Joseph answered Pharaoh and said, "Apart from God, no answer of welfare shall be given to Pharaoh."
verses.41:17: Then Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying, "In my sleep I supposed that I was standing upon the bank of the river;
verses.41:18: and as it were out of the river there came up seven cows, fair in appearance and choice in flesh, and they fed in the reed grass.
verses.41:19: And behold, seven other cows came up behind them out of the river, wretched and ugly in appearance and lean in flesh, and they fed in the reed grass—such as I have never seen uglier in all Egypt.
verses.41:20: And the seven ugly and lean cows devoured the first seven fair and choice cows,
verses.41:21: and they went into their bellies; yet it was not apparent that they had gone into their bellies, and their looks were ugly, just as at the beginning. Then I awoke and fell asleep.
verses.41:22: And I saw again in my sleep, and as it were seven ears of grain came up on one stalk, full and good.
verses.41:23: And seven other ears of grain, thin and blighted by the wind, sprang up next to them.
verses.41:24: And the seven thin and wind-blighted ears of grain swallowed up the seven good and full ears of grain. So I told the interpreters, and there was no one who could declare it to me."
verses.41:25: And Joseph said to Pharaoh, "The dream of Pharaoh is one; all that God is doing, He has shown to Pharaoh.
verses.41:26: The seven fair cows are seven years, and the seven good ears of grain are seven years; the dream of Pharaoh is one.
verses.41:27: And the seven lean cows that came up behind them are seven years, and the seven thin and wind-blighted ears of grain—they shall be seven years of famine.
verses.41:28: Now as for the word which I have spoken to Pharaoh: all that God is doing, He has shown to Pharaoh.
verses.41:29: Behold, seven years are coming of great plenty in all the land of Egypt;
verses.41:30: and seven years of famine shall come after these, and they shall forget the abundance in all the land of Egypt, and the famine shall consume the land.
verses.41:31: And the plenty shall not be recognized upon the land because of the famine that shall come after these, for it shall be exceedingly severe.
verses.41:32: And concerning the repeating of the dream to Pharaoh twice, it is because the word from God shall be true, and God will hasten to perform it.
verses.41:33: Now therefore, look out for a prudent and discerning man, and set him over the land of Egypt.
verses.41:34: And let Pharaoh act and appoint district governors over the land, and let them collect a fifth part of all the produce of the land of Egypt during the seven years of plenty,
verses.41:35: and let them gather all the food of these seven good years that are coming; and let the grain be gathered under the hand of Pharaoh, and let food be gathered in the cities.
verses.41:36: And the food shall be kept in store for the land against the seven years of famine which shall be in the land of Egypt, and the land shall not be destroyed in the famine."
verses.41:37: Now the words were pleasing in the sight of Pharaoh and in the sight of all his servants.
verses.41:38: And Pharaoh said to all his servants, "Shall we find such a man as this, who has the Spirit of God in him?"
verses.41:39: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Since God has shown you all these things, there is no man more prudent and discerning than you.
verses.41:40: You shall be over my house, and at your word all my people shall obey; only in regard to the throne will I be greater than you."
verses.41:41: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Behold, I appoint you this day over all the land of Egypt."
verses.41:42: And taking the ring from his hand, Pharaoh put it upon the hand of Joseph, and clothed him in a robe of fine linen, and placed a golden collar around his neck.
verses.41:43: And he made him ride upon the second of his chariots, and a herald made proclamation before him; and he set him over all the land of Egypt.
verses.41:44: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I am Pharaoh; without you no one shall lift up his hand in all the land of Egypt."
verses.41:45: And Pharaoh called Joseph's name Psonthomphanech; and he gave him Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of Heliopolis, to be his wife.
verses.41:46: Now Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh and went throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.41:47: And during the seven years of plenty the land brought forth sheaves.
verses.41:48: And he gathered all the food of the seven years in which there was plenty in the land of Egypt, and he laid up the food in the cities; the food of the fields of the city that were around it—On—he laid up in it.
verses.41:49: And Joseph gathered grain like the sand of the sea, exceedingly much, until he could not count it, for it was beyond number.
verses.41:50: Now to Joseph were born two sons before the seven years of famine came, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of Heliopolis, bore to him.
verses.41:51: And Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh, saying, "For God has made me forget all my toils and all that belongs to my father."
verses.41:52: And the name of the second he called Ephraim, "For God has exalted me in the land of my humiliation."
verses.41:53: Then the seven years of plenty which were in the land of Egypt passed away,
verses.41:54: and the seven years of famine began to come, just as Joseph had said. And there was famine in all the earth, and in all the land of Egypt there was no bread.
verses.41:55: And all the land of Egypt hungered, and all the people cried out to Pharaoh for bread. Then Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, "Go to Joseph, and whatever he says to you, do."
verses.41:56: And the famine was over the face of all the earth; and Joseph opened all the granaries and sold to all the Egyptians.
verses.41:57: And all the countries came to Egypt to buy from Joseph, for the famine prevailed in all the earth.
verses.42:1: Now when Jacob saw that there was selling in Egypt, he said to his sons, "Why are you idle?
verses.42:2: Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt; go down there and buy a little food for us, that we may live and not die."
verses.42:3: So the ten brothers of Joseph went down to buy grain from Egypt.
verses.42:4: But Benjamin, Joseph's brother, he did not send with his brothers; for he said, "Lest sickness befall him."
verses.42:5: And the sons of Israel came to buy with those who were coming, for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
verses.42:6: Now Joseph was ruler of the land; it was he who sold to all the people of the land. And Joseph's brothers came and bowed down before him with their faces to the ground.
verses.42:7: When Joseph saw his brothers, he recognized them, yet he acted as a stranger toward them and spoke harshly to them. And he said to them, "Where have you come from?" And they said, "From the land of Canaan to buy food."
verses.42:8: Now Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him.
verses.42:9: And Joseph remembered the dreams which he himself had seen, and he said to them, "You are spies! You have come to observe the tracks of the country."
verses.42:10: And they said, "No, my lord; your servants have come to buy food.
verses.42:11: We are all sons of one man; we are men of peace; your servants are not spies."
verses.42:12: But he said to them, "No, rather you have come to see the tracks of the land."
verses.42:13: And they said, "Your servants are twelve brothers in the land of Canaan; and behold, the youngest is with our father today, and the other is no more."
verses.42:14: Then Joseph said to them, "This is what I spoke to you, saying that you are spies.
verses.42:15: By this you shall be made manifest: by the health of Pharaoh, you shall by no means depart from here unless your youngest brother comes here.
verses.42:16: Send one from among you, and fetch your brother; and as for you, be led away until your words are made manifest, whether you speak the truth or not; otherwise, by the health of Pharaoh, surely you are spies."
verses.42:17: And he put them in prison for three days.
verses.42:18: Then he said to them on the third day, "Do this and you shall live, for I fear God:
verses.42:19: if you are men of peace, let one of your brothers be detained in the prison; but as for you, go and carry away the purchase of your grain supply,
verses.42:20: and bring your youngest brother down to me, and your words shall be believed; otherwise, you shall die." And they did so.
verses.42:21: Then each said to his brother, "Indeed, we are in sin concerning our brother, because we disregarded the distress of his soul when he pleaded with us, and we did not listen to him; for this reason this distress has come upon us."
verses.42:22: And Reuben answered and said to them, "Did I not speak to you, saying, 'Do not wrong the lad'? Yet you did not listen to me; and behold, his blood is required."
verses.42:23: Now they did not know that Joseph understood, for the interpreter was between them.
verses.42:24: And Joseph turned away from them and wept. Then he came to them again and spoke to them; and he took Simeon from them and bound him in their sight.
verses.42:25: Then Joseph commanded to fill their vessels with grain, and to restore each man's silver into his sack, and to give them provisions for the journey. And thus it was done for them.
verses.42:26: So they loaded the grain upon their donkeys and departed from there.
verses.42:27: But as one of them untied his bag to give fodder to his donkeys where they lodged, he saw the bundle of his silver, and it was at the top of the mouth of the bag.
verses.42:28: And he said to his brothers, "My silver has been restored to me, and behold, here it is in my bag!" And their hearts failed them, and they were troubled among themselves, saying, "What is this that God has done to us?"
verses.42:29: Then they came to Jacob their father in the land of Canaan, and reported to him all the things that had befallen them, saying,
verses.42:30: "The man, the lord of the land, spoke harshly to us, and put us in prison as those spying out the land.
verses.42:31: But we said to him, 'We are men of peace; we are not spies.
verses.42:32: We are twelve brothers, sons of our father; the one is no more, and the youngest is with our father today in the land of Canaan.'
verses.42:33: Then the man, the lord of the land, said to us, 'By this we shall know that you are men of peace: leave one brother here with me, and take the purchase of your grain supply and depart,
verses.42:34: and bring your youngest brother to me; then I shall know that you are not spies, but that you are men of peace. And I will restore your brother to you, and you may trade in the land.'"
verses.42:35: Now it came to pass, as they emptied their sacks, that each man's bundle of silver was in his sack; and when they and their father saw the bundles of their silver, they were afraid.
verses.42:36: And Jacob their father said to them, "You have made me childless! Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more, and you will take Benjamin! All these things have come upon me."
verses.42:37: Then Reuben spoke to his father, saying, "Slay my two sons if I do not bring him to you; give him into my hand, and I will bring him back to you."
verses.42:38: But he said, "My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he alone is left. And it will come to pass that he will fall sick along the way in which you go, and you will bring down my old age with sorrow to Hades."
verses.43:1: Now the famine grew severe upon the land.
verses.43:2: And it came to pass, when they had finished eating the grain which they had brought from Egypt, that their father said to them, "Go again and buy a little food for us."
verses.43:3: But Judah spoke to him, saying, "The man solemnly warned us, saying, 'You shall not see my face unless your youngest brother comes down to me.'
verses.43:4: If therefore you send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you;
verses.43:5: but if you do not send our brother with us, we will not go; for the man spoke to us, saying, 'You shall not see my face unless your youngest brother is with you.'"
verses.43:6: Then Israel said, "Why did you deal ill with me, reporting to the man whether you had a brother?"
verses.43:7: And they said, "The man closely questioned us concerning ourselves and our kindred, saying, 'Is your father still alive? Do you have a brother?' And we reported to him according to his questioning. Could we have known that he would say to us, 'Bring your brother'?"
verses.43:8: Then Judah said to Israel his father, "Send the lad with me, and we will arise and go, that we may live and not die, both we and you and our households.
verses.43:9: I myself will be surety for him; from my hand require him. If I do not bring him to you and set him before you, then I shall have sinned against you for all days.
verses.43:10: For if we had not delayed, by now we would have returned twice."
verses.43:11: Then Israel their father said to them, "If it is so, do this: take some of the fruits of the land in your vessels and carry down gifts to the man—some resin and some honey, incense and stacte, and terebinth and walnuts.
verses.43:12: And take double silver in your hands; the silver that was returned in your bags, return it with you; perhaps it was an oversight.
verses.43:13: Take your brother also, and arise and go down to the man.
verses.43:14: And may my God grant you favor before the man, that he may send back your one brother and Benjamin. For as for me, just as I have been made childless, I am made childless."
verses.43:15: So the men took these gifts, and they took double silver in their hands, and Benjamin; and they arose and went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
verses.43:16: When Joseph saw them, and Benjamin his brother by the same mother, he commanded the one over his house to bring the men into the house: "And slaughter beasts and make ready, for the men shall eat bread with me at noon."
verses.43:17: And the man did just as Joseph said, and he brought the men into Joseph's house.
verses.43:18: Now when the men saw that they were brought into Joseph's house, they said, "It is because of the silver that was returned in our bags the first time that we are brought in, that he may falsely accuse us and fall upon us, to take us as servants and our donkeys."
verses.43:19: So they drew near to the man who was over Joseph's house, and spoke to him at the gateway of the house,
verses.43:20: saying, "We plead with you, my lord: we came down the first time to buy food;
verses.43:21: and it came to pass, when we came to the lodging place and opened our bags, that here was each man's silver in his bag. We have now returned our silver in full weight in our bags,
verses.43:22: and other silver we have brought with us to buy food; we do not know who put the silver into our bags."
verses.43:23: But the man said to them, "Mercy be to you; do not be afraid. Your God and the God of your fathers has given you treasures in your bags; and your approved silver I have received in full." And he brought Simeon out to them.
verses.43:24: And he brought water to wash their feet, and he brought fodder for their donkeys.
verses.43:25: Then they made ready the gifts until Joseph came at noon, for they had heard that he was about to dine there.
verses.43:26: And Joseph came into the house, and they brought to him the gifts which they had in their hands into the house, and bowed down before him with their faces to the ground.
verses.43:27: Then he asked them, "How are you?" And he said to them, "Is your aged father well, of whom you spoke? Is he still alive?"
verses.43:28: And they said, "Your servant our father is well; he is still alive." And he said, "Blessed is that man by God." And they bowed low and paid homage.
verses.43:29: Then Joseph lifted up his eyes and saw Benjamin, his brother by the same mother, and said to them, "Is this your youngest brother, whom you spoke of bringing to me?" And he said, "May God have mercy on you, child."
verses.43:30: And Joseph was troubled, for his inward parts were stirred over his brother, and he sought to weep; so he went into the inner chamber and wept there.
verses.43:31: Then he washed his face, came out, and restrained himself, and said, "Set out the bread."
verses.43:32: So they set out for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians who dined with him by themselves; for the Egyptians could not eat bread together with the Hebrews, because every shepherd of sheep is an abomination to the Egyptians.
verses.43:33: And they sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright and the youngest according to his youth; and the men were astonished, each one toward his brother.
verses.43:34: And they carried a portion from him to them; and the portion of Benjamin was enlarged beyond the portions of all, fivefold compared to theirs. And they drank and became drunk with him.
verses.44:1: And Joseph commanded him who was over his house, saying, "Fill the men's sacks with provisions, as much as they are able to carry, and put each man's silver in the mouth of his sack,
verses.44:2: and put my silver cup into the sack of the youngest, and the price of his grain." And it was done according to the word of Joseph, just as he had spoken.
verses.44:3: The morning dawned, and the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.
verses.44:4: Now when they had gone out of the city and had not gone far, Joseph said to him who was over his house, saying, "Arise, pursue after the men, and you shall overtake them and say to them, 'Why have you repaid me evil for good?
verses.44:5: Why have you stolen my silver cup? Is this not the one from which my lord drinks? And he surely practices divination by it; you have accomplished evil in what you have done.'"
verses.44:6: So when he found them, he spoke to them according to these words.
verses.44:7: And they said to him, "Why does my lord speak according to these words? Far be it from your servants to do this thing.
verses.44:8: If indeed we returned to you from the land of Canaan the silver which we found in our sacks, how then would we steal silver or gold from the house of your lord?
verses.44:9: With whomever of your servants the cup is found, let him die; and we also shall be servants to our lord."
verses.44:10: And he said, "Now also as you say, so shall it be: the man with whom the cup is found, he shall be my servant, and you shall be innocent."
verses.44:11: And they hastened, and each man lowered his sack to the ground, and each man opened his sack.
verses.44:12: And he searched, beginning with the eldest until he came to the youngest; and he found the cup in Benjamin's sack.
verses.44:13: And they tore their garments, and each man placed his sack upon his donkey, and they returned to the city.
verses.44:14: Then Judah and his brethren came in to Joseph, while he was still there; and they fell to the ground before him.
verses.44:15: And Joseph said to them, "What is this deed you have done? Do you not know that a man such as I surely practices divination?"
verses.44:16: And Judah said, "What shall we answer my lord, or what shall we speak, or how shall we be justified? God has found out the iniquity of your servants. Behold, we are household servants to our lord, both we and he with whom the cup was found."
verses.44:17: And Joseph said, "Far be it from me to do this thing! The man with whom the cup was found, he shall be my servant; as for you, go up in safety to your father."
verses.44:18: Then Judah drew near to him and said, "I plead with you, my lord, let your servant speak a word before you, and do not be angry with your servant; for you are next after Pharaoh.
verses.44:19: My lord, you asked your servants, saying, 'Do you have a father or a brother?'
verses.44:20: And we said to my lord, 'We have an aged father, and a younger child of his old age; and his brother died, and he alone was left to his father, and his father has loved him.'
verses.44:21: Then you said to your servants, 'Bring him down to me, and I will care for him.'
verses.44:22: And we said to my lord, 'The boy cannot leave his father; and if he leaves his father, he will die.'
verses.44:23: But you said to your servants, 'Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you shall not see my face again.'
verses.44:24: And it came to pass when we went up to your servant, our father, that we reported to him the words of my lord.
verses.44:25: And our father said to us, 'Go again, buy us a little food.'
verses.44:26: But we said, 'We shall not be able to go down; yet if our youngest brother goes down with us, we will go down; for we shall not be able to see the face of the man if our youngest brother is not with us.'
verses.44:27: Then your servant our father said to us, 'You know that my wife bore me two sons,
verses.44:28: and the one went out from me, and you said, "He has been devoured by wild beasts," and I have not seen him since.
verses.44:29: Therefore if you take this one also from my presence, and infirmity befalls him along the way, then you will bring down my old age with sorrow to Hades.'
verses.44:30: Now therefore, if I go in to your servant, our father, and the lad is not with us, and his soul hangs upon this one's soul,
verses.44:31: then it shall come to pass, when he sees that the lad is not with us, that he will die; and your servants will bring down the old age of your servant, our father, with grief to Hades.
verses.44:32: For your servant became surety for the boy from my father, saying, 'If I do not bring him to you and set him before you, I shall have sinned against my father all my days.'
verses.44:33: Now therefore, I will remain with you as a servant in place of the boy, a household servant of my lord; and let the boy go up with his brethren.
verses.44:34: For how shall I go up to my father if the boy is not with us, lest I see the evils that will find my father?"
verses.45:1: And Joseph could not endure all those who stood by him, but he said, "Send everyone out from me!" And no one stood by Joseph any longer when Joseph made himself known to his brethren.
verses.45:2: And he uttered a cry with weeping; and all the Egyptians heard it, and it was heard in the house of Pharaoh.
verses.45:3: And Joseph said to his brethren, "I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt. Is my father still alive?" And the brethren could not answer him, for they were troubled.
verses.45:4: And he said, "I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
verses.45:5: Now therefore, do not be grieved, nor let it seem harsh to you that you sold me here; for God sent me before you for life.
verses.45:6: For this is the second year of famine upon the earth, and there remain yet five years in which there shall be neither plowing nor reaping.
verses.45:7: For God sent me before you to leave a remnant of you upon the earth, and to nourish a great survival of you.
verses.45:8: Now therefore, it was not you who sent me here, but God; and He has made me as a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and ruler of all the land of Egypt.
verses.45:9: Hasten therefore, go up to my father, and say to him, 'Thus says your son Joseph: God has made me lord of all the land of Egypt; come down therefore to me, and do not delay.
verses.45:10: And you shall dwell in the land of Goshen of Arabia, and you shall be near me—you and your sons and your sons' sons, your sheep and your cattle, and all that is yours there.
verses.45:11: And I will nourish you there—for there are still five years of famine—lest you and your sons and all your possessions be wiped out.'
verses.45:12: Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaks to you.
verses.45:13: Report therefore to my father all my glory in Egypt and all that you have seen, and make haste and bring my father down here."
verses.45:14: And falling upon the neck of Benjamin his brother, he fell upon him; and Benjamin wept upon his neck.
verses.45:15: And having kissed all his brethren, he wept over them; and after these things his brethren spoke with him.
verses.45:16: And the report was spread abroad to the house of Pharaoh, saying, "Joseph's brethren have come!" And Pharaoh and his attendants rejoiced.
verses.45:17: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Say to your brethren, 'Do this: fill your carts and depart to the land of Canaan,
verses.45:18: and taking your father and your possessions, come to me; and I will give you of all the good things of Egypt, and you shall eat the marrow of the land.'
verses.45:19: And you, command these things: to take for themselves wagons out of the land of Egypt for your little ones and wives, and taking up your father, come;
verses.45:20: and do not let your eyes spare your goods, for all the good things of Egypt shall be yours."
verses.45:21: And the sons of Israel did so. And Joseph gave them wagons according to the things spoken by Pharaoh the king, and he gave them provisions for the journey.
verses.45:22: And to all of them he gave two robes each, and to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of gold and five changes of robes.
verses.45:23: And to his father he sent in like manner, and ten donkeys carrying of all the good things of Egypt, and ten mules carrying bread for his father for the journey.
verses.45:24: So he sent his brethren away, and they departed; and he said to them, "Do not be angry along the way."
verses.45:25: And they went up out of Egypt, and came to the land of Canaan to Jacob their father,
verses.45:26: and they reported to him, saying, "Your son Joseph is alive, and he rules over all the land of Egypt." And Jacob's mind was stunned, for he did not believe them.
verses.45:27: But they spoke to him all the words spoken by Joseph, whatever he had said to them; and when he saw the wagons which Joseph had sent to take him up, the spirit of Jacob their father revived.
verses.45:28: And Israel said, "It is a great thing to me if my son Joseph is still alive; I will go and see him before I die."
verses.46:1: Now Israel departed, he and all that belonged to him, and they came to the Well of the Oath; and there he offered a sacrifice to the God of his father Isaac.
verses.46:2: And God spoke to Israel in a vision of the night, saying, "Jacob, Jacob!" And he said, "What is it?"
verses.46:3: And He said, "I am the God of your fathers; do not fear to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there.
verses.46:4: And I Myself will go down with you to Egypt, and I will bring you up again in the end; and Joseph shall lay his hands upon your eyes."
verses.46:5: Then Jacob rose up from the Well of the Oath; and the sons of Israel lifted up their father, and their dependents, and their wives onto the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him.
verses.46:6: And taking up their goods and all the possessions which they had acquired from the land of Canaan, Jacob entered into Egypt, and all his seed with him,
verses.46:7: sons and the sons of his sons with him, daughters and daughters of his sons with him; and he brought all his seed into Egypt.
verses.46:8: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel who entered into Egypt—Jacob and his sons: the firstborn of Jacob was Reuben.
verses.46:9: And the sons of Reuben were Hanoch and Phallud, Hezron and Carmi.
verses.46:10: And the sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachim, Zohar, and Samuel the son of the Canaanite woman.
verses.46:11: And the sons of Levi were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
verses.46:12: And the sons of Judah were Er, Onan, Shelom, Perez, and Zerah; but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. And the sons of Perez were Hezron and Jemuel.
verses.46:13: And the sons of Issachar were Tola, Puvah, Jasuph, and Zambram.
verses.46:14: And the sons of Zebulun were Sered, Hasron, and Jahleel.
verses.46:15: These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria, along with Dinah his daughter; all the souls, sons and daughters, were thirty-three.
verses.46:16: And the sons of Gad were Zephon, Haggi, Shuni, Thasoban, Aedis, Arodi, and Areli.
verses.46:17: And the sons of Asher were Jimnah, Jessai, Jeul, Beriah, and Saar their sister. And the sons of Beriah were Heber and Malchiel.
verses.46:18: These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah his daughter, and she bore these to Jacob—sixteen souls.
verses.46:19: And the sons of Rachel, the wife of Jacob, were Joseph and Benjamin.
verses.46:20: And sons were born to Joseph in the land of Egypt, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of Heliopolis, bore to him: Manasseh and Ephraim. And sons were born to Manasseh, whom his Syrian concubine bore to him: Machir; and Machir fathered Gilead. And the sons of Ephraim, the brother of Manasseh, were Sutalaam and Taam; and the sons of Sutalaam: Edem.
verses.46:21: And the sons of Benjamin were Bela, Chobor, and Ashbel. And the sons of Bela were Gera, Naaman, Anchis, Rosh, Mamphein, and Hophimin; and Gera fathered Arad.
verses.46:22: These are the sons of Rachel, whom Jacob fathered; all the souls were eighteen.
verses.46:23: And the sons of Dan: Hushim.
verses.46:24: And the sons of Naphtali were Jahzeel, Guni, Issaar, and Shillem.
verses.46:25: These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter, and she bore these to Jacob; all the souls were seven.
verses.46:26: Now all the souls who entered with Jacob into Egypt, those who came forth from his loins, besides the wives of the sons of Jacob, all the souls were sixty-six.
verses.46:27: And the sons of Joseph who were born to him in the land of Egypt were nine souls. All the souls of the house of Jacob who entered into Egypt were seventy-five.
verses.46:28: Now he sent Judah ahead of them to Joseph, to meet him near Heroopolis, into the land of Rameses.
verses.46:29: And Joseph yoked his chariots and went up to meet Israel his father near Heroopolis; and appearing to him, he fell upon his neck and wept with abundant weeping.
verses.46:30: And Israel said to Joseph, "From now on I may die, since I have seen your face, for you are still alive."
verses.46:31: Then Joseph said to his brethren, "I will go up and report to Pharaoh, and I will say to him, 'My brethren and the house of my father, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me;
verses.46:32: and the men are shepherds, for they have been keepers of livestock; and they have brought their livestock, and their cattle, and all that belongs to them.'
verses.46:33: Therefore, if Pharaoh calls you and says to you, 'What is your occupation?'
verses.46:34: you shall say, 'We, your servants, are keepers of livestock from youth until now, both we and our fathers,' that you may dwell in the land of Goshen of Arabia; for every shepherd of sheep is an abomination to the Egyptians."
verses.47:1: Then Joseph came and reported to Pharaoh, saying, "My father and my brethren, and their livestock and their cattle, and all that belongs to them, have come out of the land of Canaan; and behold, they are in the land of Goshen."
verses.47:2: And from among his brethren he took five men and set them before Pharaoh.
verses.47:3: And Pharaoh said to the brethren of Joseph, "What is your occupation?" And they said to Pharaoh, "Your servants are shepherds of sheep, both we and our fathers."
verses.47:5: And they said to Pharaoh, "We have come to sojourn in the land; for there is no pasture for the livestock of your servants, because the famine has grown severe in the land of Canaan. Now therefore, we shall dwell in the land of Goshen." And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Let them dwell in the land of Goshen; and if you know that there are capable men among them, appoint them rulers over my livestock." Now Jacob and his sons came into Egypt to Joseph; and Pharaoh, king of Egypt, heard of it. And Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying, "Your father and your brethren have come to you;
verses.47:6: behold, the land of Egypt is before you; settle your father and your brethren in the best of the land."
verses.47:7: Then Joseph brought in Jacob his father and set him before Pharaoh; and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
verses.47:8: And Pharaoh said to Jacob, "How many are the years of the days of your life?"
verses.47:9: And Jacob said to Pharaoh, "The days of the years of my life during which I sojourn are one hundred and thirty years; short and evil have been the days of the years of my life; they have not attained to the days of the years of the life of my fathers, in the days that they sojourned."
verses.47:10: And having blessed Pharaoh, Jacob went out from him.
verses.47:11: And Joseph settled his father and his brethren, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, just as Pharaoh had commanded.
verses.47:12: And Joseph measured out to his father, and to his brethren, and to all the house of his father, grain according to each person.
verses.47:13: Now there was no grain in all the land, for the famine grew exceedingly severe; and the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan fainted because of the famine.
verses.47:14: And Joseph gathered up all the silver that was found in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan, for the grain which they were buying, and he measured out grain to them; and Joseph brought all the silver into the house of Pharaoh.
verses.47:15: And all the silver failed from the land of Egypt and from the land of Canaan; and all the Egyptians came to Joseph, saying, "Give us bread! And why should we die before you? For our silver has failed."
verses.47:16: Then Joseph said to them, "Bring your livestock, and I will give you bread in exchange for your livestock, if your silver has failed."
verses.47:17: So they brought their livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for the horses, and for the sheep, and for the cattle, and for the donkeys; and he nourished them with bread in exchange for all their livestock in that year.
verses.47:18: Now that year passed away, and they came to him in the second year and said to him, "Let us not be wiped out from before our lord! For if our silver has failed, and our goods and our livestock have passed to you, our lord, then nothing is left to us before our lord except our own body and our land.
verses.47:19: Lest we die before you and the land become desolate, buy us and our land in exchange for bread, and we and our land will be servants of Pharaoh; give seed that we may sow and not die, and the land will become desolate."
verses.47:20: So Joseph bought all the land of the Egyptians for Pharaoh; for the Egyptians sold their land to Pharaoh, because the famine prevailed over them; and the land became Pharaoh's,
verses.47:21: and he enslaved the people to him as servants, from one end of the borders of Egypt to the other,
verses.47:22: except the land of the priests alone; Joseph did not buy this, for by a grant Pharaoh gave a gift to the priests, and they ate the portion which Pharaoh gave them; therefore they did not sell their land.
verses.47:23: Then Joseph said to all the Egyptians, "Behold, I have bought you and your land today for Pharaoh; take seed for yourselves and sow the land.
verses.47:24: And it shall be that of its produce you shall give the fifth part to Pharaoh; and the four parts shall be for yourselves, for seed for the land, and for food for you and for all your households."
verses.47:25: And they said, "You have saved us; we have found favor before our lord, and we will be servants of Pharaoh."
verses.47:26: And Joseph established it for them as an ordinance until this day over the land of Egypt, to pay a fifth to Pharaoh, except for the land of the priests alone; it did not belong to Pharaoh.
verses.47:27: So Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen; and they received an inheritance in it, and multiplied exceedingly.
verses.47:28: And Jacob lived on in the land of Egypt seventeen years; and the days of Jacob, of the years of his life, were one hundred and forty-seven years.
verses.47:29: Now the days of Israel drew near for him to die; and he called his son Joseph and said to him, "If I have found favor before you, place your hand under my thigh, and you shall show mercy and truth to me, so as not to bury me in Egypt;
verses.47:30: but I shall sleep with my fathers, and you shall carry me out of Egypt and bury me in their tomb." And he said, "I will do according to your word."
verses.47:31: And he said, "Swear to me." And he swore to him; and Israel worshiped upon the top of his staff.
verses.48:1: Now it came to pass after these things that it was reported to Joseph, "Your father is ill." And taking his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, he came to Jacob.
verses.48:2: And it was told to Jacob, saying, "Behold, your son Joseph is coming to you." And Israel gathered his strength and sat up on the bed.
verses.48:3: And Jacob said to Joseph, "My God appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan and blessed me,
verses.48:4: and He said to me, 'Behold, I will cause you to increase and multiply, and I will make you into assemblies of nations, and I will give this land to you and to your seed after you for an everlasting possession.'
verses.48:5: Now therefore your two sons who were born to you in Egypt before I came to you in Egypt are mine; Ephraim and Manasseh shall be mine, as Reuben and Simeon.
verses.48:6: But the offspring whom you may father after these shall be under the name of their brethren; they shall be called in their inheritances.
verses.48:7: And as for me, when I was coming from Mesopotamia of Syria, Rachel your mother died in the land of Canaan, as I was drawing near to the hippodrome of Chabratha of the land to come to Ephrathah; and I buried her on the road of the hippodrome—this is Bethlehem."
verses.48:8: And when Israel saw the sons of Joseph, he said, "Who are these to you?"
verses.48:9: And Joseph said to his father, "They are my sons, whom God has given me here." And Jacob said, "Bring them near to me, that I may bless them."
verses.48:10: Now the eyes of Israel were dim from old age, and he could not see. And he brought them near to him, and he kissed them and embraced them.
verses.48:11: And Israel said to Joseph, "Behold, I have not been deprived of your face; and behold, God has also shown me your seed."
verses.48:12: And Joseph brought them out from his knees, and they bowed down to him with their faces to the earth.
verses.48:13: And taking his two sons, Ephraim in his right hand, at Israel's left, and Manasseh at his left, at Israel's right, Joseph brought them near to him.
verses.48:14: And Israel stretched out his right hand and laid it upon the head of Ephraim—now he was the younger—and his left hand upon the head of Manasseh, crossing his hands.
verses.48:15: And he blessed them and said, "The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac were well-pleasing, the Lord who sustains me from youth until this day,
verses.48:16: the Angel who delivers me from all evils, may He bless these children; and my name shall be called upon them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; and may they be multiplied into a great multitude upon the earth."
verses.48:17: Now when Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, it seemed grievous to him; and Joseph took hold of his father's hand to remove it from the head of Ephraim to the head of Manasseh.
verses.48:18: And Joseph said to his father, "Not so, father, for this one is the firstborn; place your right hand upon his head."
verses.48:19: And he was unwilling, but said, "I know, child, I know. He also shall become a people, and he also shall be exalted; yet his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations."
verses.48:20: And he blessed them on that day, saying, "In you shall Israel be blessed, saying, 'May God make you as Ephraim and as Manasseh.'" And he set Ephraim before Manasseh.
verses.48:21: And Israel said to Joseph, "Behold, I am dying, and God shall be with you and bring you back to the land of your fathers.
verses.48:22: And I give to you Shechem, a choice portion above your brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorites with my sword and bow."
verses.49:1: And Jacob called his sons and said to them, "Gather together, that I may declare to you what shall befall you in the last days.
verses.49:2: Gather together and hear me, sons of Jacob; hear Israel, hear your father.
verses.49:3: Reuben, my firstborn, you are my strength and the beginning of my children—hard to bear and harsh, self-willed.
verses.49:4: You acted insolently like water—do not boil over; for you went up to your father's bed; then you defiled the couch where you went up.
verses.49:5: Simeon and Levi are brethren; they accomplished injustice by their own choice.
verses.49:6: Into their counsel may my soul not enter, and in their confederacy may my liver not contend; for in their wrath they slew men, and in their passion they hamstrung a bull.
verses.49:7: Cursed be their wrath, for it is self-willed, and their fury, for it has been hardened; I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel.
verses.49:8: Judah, may your brethren praise you; your hands shall be upon the back of your enemies; your father's sons shall bow down to you.
verses.49:9: A lion's whelp is Judah; from a shoot, my son, you have gone up. Lying down, you slept as a lion and as a whelp; who shall rouse him?
verses.49:10: A ruler shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until the things laid up for him come; and he is the expectation of the nations.
verses.49:11: Binding his colt to the vine, and the colt of his donkey to the tendril, he shall wash his robe in wine, and his garment in the blood of the grape.
verses.49:12: His eyes are more gladdening than wine, and his teeth whiter than milk.
verses.49:13: Zebulun shall dwell by the sea, and he shall be beside a haven of ships, and he shall extend as far as Sidon.
verses.49:14: Issachar desired that which is good, resting in the midst of the inheritances;
verses.49:15: and seeing the rest, that it was good, and the land, that it was fertile, he bowed his shoulder to labor and became a tiller of the soil.
verses.49:16: Dan shall judge his own people, as also one tribe in Israel.
verses.49:17: And let Dan be a serpent on the road, lying in wait upon the path, biting the heel of the horse, and the horseman shall fall backward,
verses.49:18: awaiting the salvation of the Lord.
verses.49:19: Gad—a raiding band shall raid him, yet he shall raid them at their heels.
verses.49:20: Asher—rich shall be his bread, and he shall yield delicacies to rulers.
verses.49:21: Naphtali is a spreading tree trunk, bestowing beauty in its produce.
verses.49:22: Joseph is a son increased, my envied son increased; my youngest son, return to me.
verses.49:23: Against whom, taking counsel, they railed, and masters of arrows held a grudge against him;
verses.49:24: and their bows were shattered with might, and the sinews of the arms of their hand were loosed by the hand of the Mighty One of Jacob—from there is He who strengthened Israel—from the God of your father.
verses.49:25: And my God helped you, and He blessed you with the blessing of heaven from above, and the blessing of the earth possessing all things, on account of the blessing of breasts and womb,
verses.49:26: the blessing of your father and of your mother; it has prevailed above the blessings of the enduring mountains and above the blessings of the everlasting hills. They shall be upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the brethren whom he led.
verses.49:27: Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he shall still eat, and toward evening he gives food."
verses.49:28: All these are the twelve sons of Jacob, and these things their father spoke to them; and their father blessed them, each according to his blessing he blessed them.
verses.49:29: And he said to them, "I am being gathered to my people; bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,
verses.49:30: in the double cave that is opposite Mamre in the land of Canaan, the cave which Abraham acquired from Ephron the Hittite for the possession of a tomb.
verses.49:31: There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife; there they buried Leah,
verses.49:32: in the possession of the field and of the cave that is in it, from the sons of Heth."
verses.49:33: And Jacob finished commanding his sons; and lifting up his feet onto the bed, he breathed his last and was gathered to his people.
verses.50:1: And Joseph fell upon the face of his father, wept over him, and kissed him.
verses.50:2: And Joseph commanded his servants the embalmers to embalm his father; so the embalmers embalmed Israel.
verses.50:3: And he fulfilled forty days for them, for thus the days of embalming are reckoned; and Egypt mourned for him seventy days.
verses.50:4: Now when the days of mourning had passed, Joseph spoke to the officials of Pharaoh, saying, "If I have found favor before you, speak concerning me in the ears of Pharaoh, saying,
verses.50:5: 'My father made me swear, saying, "In the tomb which I dug for myself in the land of Canaan, there you shall bury me." Now therefore I will go up and bury my father, and I will return.'"
verses.50:6: And Pharaoh said, "Go up, bury your father, just as he made you swear."
verses.50:7: So Joseph went up to bury his father; and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh and the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,
verses.50:8: and all the household of Joseph, and his brethren, and all his father's house, and his kindred; and they left behind the sheep and the cattle in the land of Goshen.
verses.50:9: And both chariots and horsemen went up with him, and the company was exceedingly great.
verses.50:10: And they came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, and they lamented for him with a great and exceedingly strong lamentation; and they observed mourning for his father seven days.
verses.50:11: And the inhabitants of the land of Canaan saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, and said, "This is a great mourning for the Egyptians." Therefore its name was called Mourning of Egypt, which is beyond the Jordan.
verses.50:12: And his sons did thus for him, and buried him there.
verses.50:13: And his sons carried him up into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the double cave, the cave which Abraham acquired for a burial possession from Ephron the Hittite, opposite Mamre.
verses.50:14: And Joseph returned to Egypt, he and his brethren and those who had gone up with him to bury his father.
verses.50:15: Now when the brethren of Joseph saw that their father was dead, they said, "Perhaps Joseph will hold a grudge against us, and will surely repay us for all the evils which we did to him."
verses.50:16: And they came to Joseph, saying, "Your father gave a sworn charge before his death, saying,
verses.50:17: 'Thus say to Joseph, "Forgive them their unrighteousness and their sin, for they did wicked things to you."' And now, pardon the unrighteousness of the servants of the God of your father." And Joseph wept while they spoke to him.
verses.50:18: And coming to him, they said, "Behold, we are household servants."
verses.50:19: And Joseph said to them, "Do not be afraid, for I belong to God.
verses.50:20: You purposed against me for evil, but God purposed concerning me for good, so that it might come to pass as it is this day, that a great people might be nourished."
verses.50:21: And he said to them, "Do not be afraid; I will nourish you and your households." And he comforted them and spoke to their heart.
verses.50:22: And Joseph dwelt in Egypt, he and his brethren and all his father's household; and Joseph lived one hundred and ten years.
verses.50:23: And Joseph saw children of Ephraim to the third generation; and the sons of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were born upon the thighs of Joseph.
verses.50:24: And Joseph spoke to his brethren, saying, "I am dying; but God will surely visit you, and will bring you up out of this land to the land which God swore to our fathers, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob."
verses.50:25: And Joseph made the sons of Israel swear, saying, "In the visitation with which God will visit you, you shall also carry up my bones from here with you."
verses.50:26: And Joseph died, being one hundred and ten years old; and they embalmed him, and placed him in the coffin in Egypt.

notes.1:1: The Greek reads epoiesen ('made') and singular ton ouranon ('heaven'), distinct from the Hebrew 'created the heavens.'
notes.1:2: Greek aoratos kai akataskeuastos literally means 'unseen and unformed/unfurnished,' reflecting the Septuagint's own rendering of the Hebrew pair.
notes.1:6: Greek stereoma denotes a firm, solid expanse ('firmament').
notes.1:9: The second half of the verse, explicitly narrating the waters gathering into their gatherings and the dry land appearing, is a Septuagint plus retained from the Greek text.
notes.1:30: Greek psychen zoes literally means 'a soul of life,' rendered literally here to distinguish the genitive phrase from 'living soul' (psyche zosa) in verses 20 and 24.
notes.2:2: The Septuagint reads 'on the sixth day' (en te hemera te hekte), whereas the Masoretic Hebrew text reads 'on the seventh day.'
notes.2:7: Greek reads 'into his face' (eis to prosopon autou), where the Hebrew specifies 'into his nostrils.'
notes.2:8: Greek paradeisos ('paradise,' an enclosed park or orchard) is the Septuagint's regular term for Eden's garden.
notes.2:16: In the Greek text, the Lord addresses Adam in the second-person singular in verse 16 (phage) and shifts to the second-person plural in verse 17 (phagesthe ... apothaneisthe).
notes.2:18: The Greek reads first-person plural poiesomen ('let Us make'), echoing 1:26, where the Hebrew has singular 'I will make.'
notes.3:15: The Greek reads masculine autos ('he') with the verb teresei ('shall watch for' or 'lie in wait for'), distinct from both the Hebrew ('bruise/crush') and the Latin Vulgate ('she shall crush').
notes.3:16: Greek apostrophe means 'turning' (or 'recourse'), where the Hebrew reads 'desire.'
notes.3:17: Greek reads 'in your labors/works' (en tois ergois sou), reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants than Masoretic 'because of you.'
notes.3:20: The Septuagint translates Hebrew Hawwah ('Eve') directly into Greek as Zoe ('Life'), preserving the wordplay with 'all the living.'
notes.4:7: The Septuagint reads this difficult verse in terms of rightly offering and rightly dividing a sacrifice, followed by "Be still; to you shall be his turning," differing notably from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's imagery of sin crouching at the door.
notes.4:16: The Greek text reads "Naid," corresponding to "Nod" in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.4:18: The Greek text preserves the distinct name forms "Gaidad" (Hebrew "Irad"), "Maiel" (Hebrew "Mehujael"), and "Methuselah" (the same name as in 5:21, where Hebrew has "Methushael").
notes.4:22: The Greek text reads simply "Tubal" (Thobel), without the "-cain" element found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("Tubal-cain").
notes.4:26: The Greek text reads "This man hoped to call upon the name of the Lord God," reflecting a different understanding of the Hebrew verb than the Masoretic Text ("then men began to call").
notes.5:3: Throughout Genesis 5, the Septuagint preserves a longer patriarchal chronology than the Hebrew Masoretic Text, often giving an age one hundred years higher at the birth of the named son (here two hundred and thirty years rather than one hundred and thirty) with a corresponding reduction in the remaining years.
notes.5:24: The Greek reads "was well-pleasing to God" (also in 5:22) and "he was not found, because God transferred him," wording quoted directly in Hebrews 11:5.
notes.5:28: For Lamech, the Septuagint records one hundred and eighty-eight years before Noah's birth, five hundred and sixty-five years afterward (5:30), and seven hundred and fifty-three years in total (5:31), compared with one hundred and eighty-two, five hundred and ninety-five, and seven hundred and seventy-seven in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.5:29: The Greek renders Lamech's wordplay on Noah's name with "give us rest" (dianapausei), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "comfort us."
notes.6:2: The Greek reads "the angels of God" (hoi angeloi tou theou) here, whereas verse 4 reads "the sons of God" (hoi huioi tou theou), reflecting an ancient Septuagint interpretive tradition identifying these beings as angelic.
notes.6:6: Rather than describing God as repenting or grieving, the Greek uses two verbs of reflection—enethymēthē ("laid it to heart") and dienoēthē ("pondered it")—and in verse 7 uses ethymōthēn ("I am angered").
notes.6:14: The Greek specifies "squared timbers" (xylōn tetragōnōn) rather than Hebrew "gopher wood," and renders "compartments" literally as "nests" (nossias).
notes.6:16: The Greek participle episynagōn ("tapering it together") describes the ark as narrowing upward to a one-cubit crown rather than specifying a window or roof opening.
notes.7:4: The rare Greek noun anastema (literally "that which rises" or "stands," rendered "living being") also appears in verse 23 to encompass all living creatures upon the earth.
notes.7:11: The Greek dates the onset of the flood to the twenty-seventh day of the second month—and likewise the ark's resting in 8:4 to the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month—differing from the seventeenth day in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.8:2: The Greek text here reads apekalyphthēsan ("were uncovered"), whereas other Septuagint witnesses read epekalyphthēsan ("were covered over" or "closed"), agreeing with the Hebrew sense of shutting off the waters.
notes.8:5: The Greek places the sighting of the mountain summits in the eleventh month, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text dates it to the tenth month.
notes.8:7: The Greek explicitly states that the raven "did not return" (ouch hypestrepsen) until the water dried up, differing from the Hebrew reading that it went out to and fro.
notes.8:22: The Greek pairs "summer and spring" (theros kai ear) rather than "summer and winter," and places "day and night" (hēmeran kai nykta) in the adverbial accusative modifying "shall not cease."
notes.9:1: The Greek text includes the closing command "and have dominion over it," echoing Genesis 1:28, which does not appear in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.9:6: Where the Hebrew reads "by man shall his blood be shed; for in the image of God He made man," the Greek reads "in return for his blood shall it be shed" and uses the first-person verb "I made."
notes.9:21: The Greek reads "in his house" (and "in the houses of Shem" in verse 27), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "tent" and "tents."
notes.9:25: The Greek renders the superlative Hebrew idiom "a servant of servants" as "a house servant" (pais oiketes).
notes.10:2: The Greek includes Elishah among the sons of Japheth here as well as among the sons of Javan in verse 4; in verse 4, the Greek also reads "the Rhodians" where the Hebrew reads Dodanim.
notes.10:8: In verses 8–9, the Greek describes Nimrod as a "giant" (gigas) rather than "mighty one," and in verse 9 adds "God" to the first occurrence of "the Lord."
notes.10:12: The Greek reads the city name "Dasem" where the Hebrew reads Resen; similarly, in verse 19 the Greek reads "Dasa" where the Hebrew reads Lasha.
notes.10:24: Following the Septuagint genealogy echoed in Luke 3:36, the Greek includes Cainan between Arphaxad and Shelah.
notes.10:28: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which lists Obal before Abimael, the Greek lists only Abimael and Sheba in this verse; in verse 23, the Greek also reads "Meshech" (Mosoch) where the Hebrew has Mash.
notes.11:9: The Greek text translates the name of the tower as "Confusion" (Synchysis) rather than transliterating "Babel," matching the verb "confounded" in the same verse and the mention of both "the city and the tower" in verse 8.
notes.11:12: The Septuagint genealogy includes an additional generation, Cainan (cf. Luke 3:36), along with distinct patriarchal ages and the closing refrain "and died" for each patriarch.
notes.11:28: Here and in verse 31 the Greek reads "the country of the Chaldeans," without the city name "Ur" found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.11:29: Here and through chapter 16 the Greek text spells her name "Sara" (later changed to "Sarra" in 17:15), rendered with the standard English pre-renaming form "Sarai."
notes.12:2: The Greek reads "and you shall be blessed" (an adjective describing Abram's state), whereas the Hebrew text reads "and be a blessing."
notes.12:6: The Greek renders the location as "the high oak," interpreting rather than transliterating the Hebrew name "Moreh."
notes.12:16: The Greek uses the plural "they dealt well" and lists "calves" and "mules," where the Hebrew text has the singular "he dealt well" with "oxen" and "female donkeys."
notes.13:4: This Greek text reads "where he had made the tent" (ten skenen), a variant reading preserved in Septuagint witnesses alongside "at the beginning" (ten archen).
notes.13:14: "West" renders Greek thalassan, literally "sea" (the Mediterranean Sea), the standard biblical directional idiom for west (as also in 12:8).
notes.13:16: The Greek compares Abram's offspring to "the sand of the earth" rather than "the dust of the earth" as in the Hebrew text, and verse 17 adds "and to your seed forever."
notes.14:1: The Greek reads "in the reign of Amraphel" (MT: "in the days of") and presents distinct forms of several royal names here and in v. 2: Thalga (v. 9: Thalgal; MT: Tidal), Balla (Bera), Barsa (Birsha), Sennaar (Shinab), Symobor (Shemeber), and Balak (Bela).
notes.14:5: The Greek translates Rephaim as "giants," renders "the Zuzim in Ham" as "strong nations together with them," and reads "the Somites" (corresponding to MT "the Emim") in "the city of Shaveh" (translating Kiriathaim as "the city").
notes.14:11: Here and in vv. 16 and 21, the Greek reads "cavalry" (collective feminine hippos), reflecting a Hebrew reading meaning "steeds" rather than the Masoretic "goods/possessions."
notes.14:13: The Greek renders "the Hebrew" etymologically as "the migrant" (perates, one who crosses over) and gives the ally's name as Aunan (MT: Aner); similarly, v. 15 reads Chobal where the MT has Hobah.
notes.14:22: The Greek uses the future tense "I will stretch out" (MT: "I have lifted") and reads "God Most High" without "the Lord."
notes.15:2: The Greek takes Masek as the personal name of Abram's homeborn maidservant ("the son of Masek my homeborn maidservant"), differing from the difficult Masoretic phrase usually rendered "heir/steward of my house."
notes.15:6: The Greek specifies "Abram believed God" (MT: "he believed the LORD") and uses the passive verb "it was reckoned" (MT: active "He counted"), the wording quoted in the New Testament (Rom. 4:3; Gal. 3:6; Jas. 2:23).
notes.15:11: The Greek reads "Abram sat down with them," reflecting a different Hebrew verbal root ("sit") than the Masoretic Text ("drove them away").
notes.15:15: The Greek text here reads trapheis ("nourished") rather than tapheis ("buried," as in the MT and some Greek witnesses).
notes.15:19: "Kelmonites" preserves the Greek textual form corresponding to the Masoretic "Kadmonites"; in v. 21 the Greek also adds "the Hivites," bringing the list of nations to eleven.
notes.16:1: The Greek spells her name Sara here (distinguished from Sarra after the name change in Genesis 17:15), rendered with the standard English pre-covenant spelling Sarai.
notes.16:2: The Greek uses the second-person verb "that you may have children by her," whereas the Masoretic Text has the first-person "that I may obtain children by her."
notes.16:7: This Greek text reads "the angel of the Lord God," whereas the Masoretic Text and many Greek witnesses read simply "the angel of the Lord."
notes.16:13: The Greek clarifies the difficult Hebrew saying as "I have seen face to face Him who appeared to me," and in v. 14 translates the well's name accordingly ("The Well of Him Whom I Saw Face to Face," MT: Beer-lahai-roi).
notes.17:1: The Greek text reads "I am your God" rather than the Hebrew "God Almighty" (El Shaddai), and renders "walk before Me" as "be well-pleasing before Me."
notes.17:14: The Greek text includes the phrase "on the eighth day," which is absent from the Masoretic Hebrew text.
notes.17:15: The Greek text distinguishes the old and new names as Sara and Sarra, doubling the r rather than changing from Hebrew Sarai to Sarah.
notes.17:16: Unlike the Hebrew text, which uses feminine pronouns referring to Sarah, the Greek uses masculine pronouns ("bless him ... he shall become nations ... from him"), directing the second blessing to the promised child.
notes.17:20: The Greek reads "twelve nations" rather than the Hebrew "twelve princes."
notes.18:1: The Greek reads "God," the singular "oak of Mamre," and "at midday" rather than the Hebrew "YHWH," "oaks of Mamre," and "in the heat of the day."
notes.18:5: The Greek uses the singular verb "He said" here and in verse 9, highlighting the Lord as the chief speaker among the three visitors.
notes.18:12: Instead of the Hebrew question about experiencing pleasure in old age, the Greek reads literally, "It has not yet happened to me until now, and my lord is old."
notes.18:30: The Greek opens with the elliptical deferential plea "Not anything, Lord" (repeated in verse 32), rendered here as "Do not be displeased, Lord."
notes.19:4: In the Greek text, "before lying down" completes the sentence from verse 3 ("and they ate before lying down"), rather than introducing the gathering of the men of Sodom as in the Masoretic Text.
notes.19:16: The Greek text reads "and they were troubled" and "took hold of their hand" (with plural verbs and pronoun), whereas the Masoretic Text describes Lot lingering and the messengers seizing his hand.
notes.19:18: Although Lot speaks to both angels ("to them"), he addresses them with the singular vocative "lord" (Greek kyrie), and the dialogue continues in the singular through verse 22.
notes.19:38: The Septuagint preserves the distinct name "Amman" with the explanatory gloss "the son of my kindred" (and "Ammanites"), corresponding to Hebrew Ben-Ammi and paralleling the explanatory etymology added in verse 37 ("From my father").
notes.20:2: The Greek text includes an explicit explanatory clause absent from the Masoretic Text: "for he feared to say, 'She is my wife,' lest the men of the city slay him on her account."
notes.20:4: The Septuagint reads "an unwitting and righteous nation" (Greek agnooun), emphasizing Abimelech's innocence through ignorance, where the Masoretic Text reads "even a righteous nation."
notes.20:14: The Greek text adds "a thousand didrachmas" here (anticipating verse 16) and reads the earlier name form "Abram" rather than "Abraham."
notes.20:16: The Septuagint renders Abimelech's words distinctly as "a thousand didrachmas" given "for the honor of your countenance and for all the women with you," closing with the imperative "speak the truth in all things."
notes.21:6: The Greek reads "will rejoice with me" (synchareitai moi) rather than "will laugh with me," emphasizing Sarah's joyful vindication; in v. 7 the Greek also reads "in my old age" rather than "in his old age."
notes.21:9: The Greek explicitly adds "with her own son Isaac," specifying with whom Ishmael was playing.
notes.21:16: Whereas the Hebrew has Hagar lift up her voice and weep, the Greek attributes the crying aloud and weeping to the child, directly preparing for God's hearing the child's voice in v. 17; likewise, v. 15 specifies a fir tree and v. 19 specifies living water.
notes.21:22: Both here and in v. 32 the Greek includes Ahuzzath (Greek Ochozath), Abimelech's bridal escort (nymphagogos), who appears only in Genesis 26:26 in the Hebrew text.
notes.21:31: Here the Greek translates Beersheba as "Well of Swearing" (Phrear horkismou), and in vv. 14, 32, 33, and 22:19 as "the Well of the Oath"; in v. 33 the Greek also renders the Hebrew tamarisk tree as "a field" (aroura).
notes.22:2: The Greek renders the land of Moriah descriptively as "the high land" (ten gen ten hypselen) and refers to Isaac as Abraham's "beloved son" (agapeton) rather than his "only son."
